referenceMap.heroPattern: Full-width split-to-stacked hero with brand/logo block, bold H1, short supporting paragraph, and a compact benefit list with tick icons beneath the headline; primary conversion is presented through a nearby lead form rather than a hero button.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-purpose sections stacked vertically with clear topic headers, then dense feature grids; the page favors a linear sales flow: hero, form, product capabilities, then deeper feature explanation. Content appears grouped in cards/blocks with consistent spacing rather than nested complex layouts.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple bordered/white cards with minimal decoration, functional rather than glossy; likely modest radius, subtle shadow or border, and strong header hierarchy. No evidence of glassmorphism or heavy visual treatment.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA is form-led conversion; if buttons exist, they are likely simple, high-contrast, and repeated sparingly. The page pattern emphasizes lead capture with a form card over multiple competing CTAs.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing pattern detected from the provided reference.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in the provided reference; likely standard corporate footer if present, but no reusable evidence from the snippet.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Logo-first hero with minimal imagery in the visible area; media is utility-driven rather than promotional. Supporting icons are small and used as list markers, not as feature illustrations.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Feature-led modular sections with labeled headers, headline, short descriptive paragraph, and multiple feature items beneath. Best reused as a stacked capabilities grid with concise titles and one-line descriptions, optionally grouped into thematic sections.
referenceMap.formPattern: Prominent lead-generation card placed immediately after the hero, containing a section title and a multi-field form with hidden tracking inputs. Pattern favors captured intent early in the page with form-centric conversion.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No strong motion system is evident in the reference; treat as mostly static marketing layout with possible minor library-driven enhancements only if implemented elsewhere.
designNotes: Use a high-contrast hero with one dominant message and three supporting proof points.
Place conversion form immediately after the hero to reduce friction.
Keep feature descriptions short and scannable; avoid long paragraphs.
Use simple iconography and restrained visual styling for a B2B enterprise feel.
Prefer vertical reading flow and modular sections over interactive content discovery patterns.
Maintain consistent container widths and generous vertical spacing between major sections.

personality.buyer: Administrators, IT teams, MSSPs, and security-conscious organizations
personality.emotion: controlled urgency, trust, technical clarity, operational confidence
personality.reasoning: Firewall Analyzer is a security operations product focused on monitoring, compliance, log analysis, and policy control. The visual language should feel precise and authoritative, with strong structure, high contrast, and dashboard-like intelligence. Brand colors from Techjockey can be used to add warmth and recognizability, but the overall personality must stay enterprise-security led, not salesy or playful.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The hero headline is long, so it needs a compact but strong size to preserve hierarchy without wrapping awkwardly.

colours.colourReason: Primary must come directly from Techjockey brand orange and power the hero background and primary CTA. Black, white, and soft grey from the brand palette create the security-grade contrast needed for monitoring, compliance, and log-heavy interfaces.

backgroundSystem.hero: solid #ff6b00 with subtle dark overlay strips and white type

layout.heroBackground: Brand orange hero with a layered dashboard visual on the right and strong white typography on the left.
layout.heroReason: This product benefits from an operational split hero: clear value proposition on the left, a simulated firewall analytics dashboard or log monitoring UI on the right to immediately signal technical credibility.
layout.featureReason: The content has two strong feature clusters plus supporting features. Use a spotlight intro block, then a clean card grid for specific capabilities, and a second contrasting section for deeper trust/compliance benefits.
layout.darkSectionFor: Hero only, plus optional slim proof band or stats strip in deep charcoal to intensify contrast and improve readability.

personality.imageryDirection: Use a high-clarity product-style visual rather than abstract stock photography: firewall dashboard screens, log tables, traffic graphs, alert panels, and compliance cards layered in a polished UI collage. If a real screenshot is unavailable, build a CSS-based interface mockup with metric tiles, activity lines, threat badges, and terminal-like log rows. Add floating chips for 'Real-time Monitoring', 'Compliance Audit', 'Traffic Analysis', and 'Rule Optimization'.
personality.designPersonality: Technical, structured, and premium-operational. The page should feel like a control room for firewall intelligence: sharp grids, clear hierarchy, compact data cards, and confident orange-led brand presence. Avoid playful illustrations, soft consumer aesthetics, or generic SaaS gradients. Make it feel like a serious tool for admins and MSSPs, while still polished and conversion-oriented.

componentNeeds.variantHint: dark security hero with strong headline hierarchy and compact CTA area
componentNeeds.notes: Use bold H1 sized down for long copy, short subheadline, and a primary CTA button. No secondary CTA is available. Keep layout authoritative and uncluttered.
Since no supporting line exists, use a concise 2-3 point value-support list only if needed for clarity; keep it visually light.
5 features should be arranged as a 3-column desktop grid with two rows, single column on mobile. Emphasize clear titles and one-line descriptions.
Use the provided compatibility headline as the main framing statement; keep the supporting description concise and technical.

componentNeeds.variantHint: 4-item grid with compliance and control benefits
componentNeeds.notes: Present as a clean comparative value section, not a marketing-heavy block. Keep icons functional and consistent.

componentNeeds.variantHint: 5-item support grid or split grid with emphasis on ROI/value
componentNeeds.notes: This section should feel like expansion evidence: cost, deployment speed, reporting, ROI, and device coverage. Avoid visual repetition by varying card emphasis slightly.
Use star rating treatment only if provided by the design system, but do not invent numeric ratings. Preserve quote, author, designation, and company clearly.

layoutStrategy.hero: Use a full-width dark hero with strong hierarchy and a single high-contrast primary CTA. Since no product screenshot is supplied, keep it text-led and optionally use subtle technical visual cues rather than imagery. Prioritize immediate clarity over density.
layoutStrategy.features: Stack features in clean white cards with consistent spacing and light borders. Start with compatibility proof, then core monitoring capabilities, then investigation and policy management. Keep the section scannable and modular.
layoutStrategy.proof: Use testimonials as the main proof layer because trust badges, customer counts, awards, and news are not available. Treat this as social validation rather than a promotional banner.
layoutStrategy.pricing: Do not show pricing because no pricing data exists in the input. Preserve the page as a product evaluation and lead-generation journey without introducing speculative cost anchors.
layoutStrategy.form: Do not include a lead form. The available CTA should function as the only conversion trigger, with an emphasis on button placement and repeated CTA discipline rather than form-led capture.

designIntent.tokenProfileHint: Security product profile: use Rajdhani for headings and Inter for body; favor a trust-authority palette with a dark navy hero, white content sections, subtle borders, and restrained motion. Keep cards functional, 12px radius, and lightly elevated only on hover.
designIntent.figmaReadySummary: Plan a single-product security landing page with a dark, high-authority hero, one primary CTA, and no form. Follow with a compatibility-first feature grid, a benefits section focused on control and compliance, an additional value section for ROI and reporting, and testimonial proof at the end. Use clean bordered cards, dense but scannable content, and enterprise-grade spacing to support IT evaluators.

figmaBuildPlan.tokenProfileHint: Security category: use Rajdhani for headings and Inter for body; apply trust-authority colour mode with dark hero, white text, and accent CTA. Keep sections modular, card-based, and utility-focused.

Use 2 testimonial cards on desktop since only two quotes are supplied. Keep the section background very light grey or subtly tinted for separation. No additional testimonial content should be invented.
